what: Align Technology makes Invisalign, the clear plastic aligners that straighten teeth instead of metal braces, and the iTero scanners dentists use to take a digital impression of a mouth.
customers: Orthodontists and general dentists, who buy the aligners and prescribe them to patients.
money: Invisalign treatments sold to dental practices
moat: Twenty-five years of treatment data and software that predicts how teeth will move, plus scanners installed in practices that feed cases straight into the Invisalign workflow.
risks: Revenue has been flat around $4.0B for four years: the growth phase has ended for now
Orthodontic treatment is discretionary and often financed, so it suffers when credit tightens
Patents on the core technology have expired and cheaper aligners are entering
opportunities: 23 times earnings with $1.1B of cash against $114M of debt
A 10.2% net margin and $603M of free cash flow
Only a fraction of the world's orthodontic cases are treated with clear aligners, and teenagers are the largest untapped group
watch: Clear aligner case volumes, particularly teenage cases.
